question: On 12 open research questions, does the AIL+MoIE five-stage procedure (C4) produce hypotheses rated more novel by a blind judge than compute-matched best-of-n versions of few-shot (C1-bon), chain-of-thought (C2-bon) and tree-of-thoughts (C3-bon) prompting, using the same generator model (Claude Haiku) and the same total token budget, judged by Claude Sonnet and Claude Opus?
hypothesis: H1c: the AIL+MoIE procedure rates more novel than each compute-matched best-of-n baseline. Primary hypothesis of the Hermes12 pre-registration, in the lab's second instrument (ail-moie-h1c-001), configured here with a Claude Haiku generator and Claude Sonnet and Opus judges.
matching: Per question, budget B is the mean total tokens of C4 over its repetitions, where input tokens are estimated as characters divided by 4 of the experiment prompt (excluding the CLI's fixed per-call scaffolding, about 850 tokens measured) and output tokens are as reported by the API. For each baseline, n is the largest integer such that n single passes plus one selector call fit within B; the selector call is charged to the baseline. The report states the achieved cost ratio.

judges.description: claude sonnet via the claude CLI, same adapter as the generator
claude opus via the claude CLI, same adapter as the generator

primary.test: one-sided paired sign-flip permutation across questions; Hedges g from per-question differences

falsification: H1c is NOT supported if any of the three contrasts has Holm-adjusted p of 0.05 or more, or Hedges g of 0.5 or less. If judge agreement (Krippendorff alpha for novelty) is below 0.4, the result is inconclusive, not supported. A tie is not supported. Inherited from the Hermes12 pre-registration: if H1c fails across two independent replications the integration claim is reported as false; the lab decides whether this run counts as one of the two. Independence is NOT met in this configuration (generator and both judges are Claude models). A NOT SUPPORTED result stands. A SUPPORTED result does not establish the claim and requires replication with judges from another family or with human raters.
limits: The standard is a rubric applied by a model judge. It is weaker than an executable check and measures what a judge rates as novel, which is not the same as what is novel or true.

If a judge is the same model or family as the generator, self-preference bias can inflate ratings; the analysis flags a judge that used the same adapter, and the registered requirement is a different family.
12 author-written questions and 2 repetitions per question is a small sample. With 12 questions the registered rule has limited power to detect a modest effect (see controls.json).
C5 (the retrieval-backed MoIE arm) and hypotheses H2 and H3 of the original package are not tested here; coherence non-inferiority is reported as a secondary check only.
The Positive Deviant Scout uses the model's own knowledge, so cited anomalies are not verified and may be invented; the scout prompt asks the model not to invent cases.
One generator model is tested. A result says nothing about other models.
Blinding hides arm labels but not writing style; a judge may be able to guess which arm produced a text.

The generator's context window must be large enough that MoIE's accumulated stage context is not truncated; the Ollama adapter is run with OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=8192 and fails closed if a prompt fills the window.

Independence requirement not met: the generator and both judges are Claude models from one vendor, so shared training lineage and self-preference can inflate or distort ratings in an unknown direction.
The claude CLI exposes no seed or temperature. Outputs are not exactly reproducible, and results come from one run.
Token accounting excludes the CLI's fixed per-call scaffolding and estimates input tokens from characters; compute matching is therefore approximate.
The run was executed and judged by an AI assistant in a cloud session at the owner's instruction, with generation and judging calls made automatically; the owner did not supervise individual calls.
One generator model (Haiku) is tested. The result says nothing about other models, including the owner's local models.
If interrupted, the run may be resumed with the same adapter; every resume is recorded in RUN.json.
stopping_rule: One revision pass to prompts and questions after the controls pass, then lock. No edits after lock; a change means a new experiment directory. The pre-registration was locked and committed before any generation call.

generator.model: claude haiku via the claude CLI (alias haiku; the adapter log records the resolved model id)
generator.temperature_and_seed: not controllable through the CLI; the CLI default applies and runs are not exactly reproducible
generator.working_directory: an empty temporary directory, tools disabled, so no project instructions are loaded
